context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform designed for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It ensures EU-only data residency while delivering high-performance catalog searches and seamless external integrations.

## Key Elements
* Library Management System (Core Software System)
* Library Patron (External User via Self-Service Portal)
* Librarian / Library Staff (External User via Admin Portal)
* Identity Provider / IdS (External System for authentication)
* Payment Gateway (External System for fine processing)
* Notification Service (External System for Email/SMS alerts via SendGrid/Twilio)
* Digital Content Repository / DRM Provider (External System for e-books/audiobooks)

## Relationships
* Library Patron -> Library Management System via HTTPS (Self-Service Portal)
* Librarian -> Library Management System via HTTPS (Admin Portal)
* Library Management System -> Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST
* Library Management System -> Notification Service via HTTPS/REST API
* Library Management System -> Digital Content Repository via HTTPS/REST and LTI/OAuth

## Technology Stack
* HTTPS/REST: Standard protocol for all internal and external portal and service communications
* LTI/OAuth: Protocol for digital content repository license verification
* External Payment Gateway: Selected to handle PCI-DSS scope outside the core boundary
* External Identity Provider: Selected to enforce EU-only data residency for user identities

## Rationale
This architecture meets performance and data residency requirements by offloading sensitive and heavy workloads to specialized external systems. Utilizing isolated micro-integrations and secure HTTPS/REST protocols ensures compliance with EU data constraints while easily achieving sub-800ms search responses.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It ensures strict EU-only data residency while delivering high-performance catalog searches.

## Key Elements
* Library Patron and Librarian / Library Staff (Users)
* Web Application Container (React, TypeScript)
* API Gateway Container (Kong or NGINX)
* Core Domain Container (Java, Spring Boot)
* Search Container (Elasticsearch)
* Integration Worker Container (Node.js/Python)
* Message Broker Container (RabbitMQ)
* PostgreSQL Database (EU-hosted)
* External Systems: Identity Provider / IdS, Payment Gateway, Notification Service, Digital Content Repository / DRM Provider

## Relationships
* Web Application to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST and WebSockets
* API Gateway to internal containers via gRPC and internal REST
* Core Domain to PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch via native TCP drivers over TLS
* Core Domain to Message Broker (RabbitMQ) via AMQP over TLS
* Integration Worker to external Payment Gateway and Notification Service

## Technology Stack
* React with TypeScript: Powers the frontend web application container
* Java with Spring Boot: Implements the reliable Core Domain container logic
* Elasticsearch: Dedicated engine to meet the <800ms search latency requirement
* PostgreSQL: EU-hosted relational database for transactional data integrity
* RabbitMQ: Asynchronous message broker to decouple workflows and integrations
* Kong or NGINX: API Gateway for secure routing, SSL termination, and rate limiting

## Rationale
This containerized architecture isolates the search workload into Elasticsearch to easily achieve the required sub-800ms response times. Additionally, hosting all databases and message brokers within the EU guarantees full compliance with strict data residency constraints.

Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within the EU. The Web Application container is decomposed into modular frontend components to ensure high-performance discovery and circulation.

## Key Elements
* Library Patron and Librarian / Library Staff (Users)
* Web Application (React, TypeScript Container)
* Routing & Shell Component
* Catalog & Search Component
* Circulation & Self-Service Component
* API Client Service
* API Gateway (Kong or NGINX), Core Domain (Java, Spring Boot), and Search Engine (Elasticsearch)

## Relationships
* Library Patron & Librarian -> Web Application: Accesses portals [HTTPS]
* Web Application -> API Gateway: Routes requests [HTTPS/REST and WebSockets]
* Routing & Shell -> Catalog & Search & Circulation & Self-Service: Delegates views
* Catalog & Search -> TanStack Query -> API Client Service: Fetches data [HTTPS/REST]
* Domain components -> API Client Service: Communicates with backend [HTTPS/REST and WebSockets]

## Technology Stack
* React with TypeScript: Enforces type safety and structured SPA navigation
* TanStack Query: Provides client-side caching and input debouncing to meet performance constraints
* Axios/Fetch: Handles HTTP transport
* WebSockets: Streams real-time notifications

## Rationale
This architecture decouples UI domain logic from network transport while implementing client-side caching to guarantee 99th-percentile search response times under 800ms. It maintains strict EU data residency constraints through localized integration patterns.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patron & Librarian**: End users accessing the system.
- **Web Application**: React and TypeScript frontend.
- **API Gateway**: Kong or NGINX container comprising:
  - Routing & Proxy Engine (Kong/NGINX Core)
  - Authentication & Authorization Filter (Lua/OpenResty, JWT)
  - Rate Limiting & Throttling Module (Redis-backed)
  - SSL/TLS Termination & Security Headers Module (OpenSSL/NGINX)
  - Request Transformation & Analytics Filter (Lua/Go)
- **Core Domain**: Java, Spring Boot microservices.
- **Search Engine**: Elasticsearch for cataloging and search.
- **Integration Worker**: Node.js/Python background processor.
- **Message Broker**: RabbitMQ for asynchronous messaging.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: Relational datastore.
- **External Systems**: Identity Provider (IdS), Payment Gateway, Notification Service, DRM Provider.

## Relationships
- Web Application -> SSL/TLS Termination & Security Headers Module: Entry point for traffic [HTTPS]
- SSL/TLS Termination & Security Headers Module -> Authentication & Authorization Filter: Forwards decrypted traffic
- Authentication & Authorization Filter -> Routing & Proxy Engine: Forwards validated requests
- Routing & Proxy Engine -> Core Domain: Proxies internal traffic [gRPC and internal REST]
- Routing & Proxy Engine -> Search Engine: Direct internal queries for performance [gRPC/REST]

## Technology Stack
- React / TypeScript: Frontend UI for responsive user experience.
- Kong / NGINX: API Gateway for secure routing, SSL termination, and rate limiting.
- Java / Spring Boot: Core business logic with robust enterprise capabilities.
- Elasticsearch: High-speed search engine supporting <800ms response SLA.
- PostgreSQL: Relational storage enforcing EU data residency constraints.
- RabbitMQ: Asynchronous messaging between core and integration workers.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the presentation layer from backend services using a high-performance API Gateway to meet strict latency and security goals. Microservices and dedicated search components ensure scalability while adhering to EU-only data residency constraints.

Core Domain.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Domain container is a modular Spring Boot application designed to manage library item cataloguing, circulation logic, and search synchronisation. It ensures reliable transactional integrity while meeting strict EU data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
* **Catalog Management Component**: Handles physical and digital item cataloguing (R-01).
* **Circulation Engine Component**: Manages loans, reservations, and business invariants.
* **Event Publisher Component**: Asynchronously emits domain events using Spring AMQP.
* **Search Synchronizer Component**: Updates the search index to achieve < 800 ms search responses (R-05).
* **PostgreSQL Database**: Stores transactional domain data locally.
* **Search Engine**: Externalized index providing fast catalog queries.
* **Message Broker**: Handles asynchronous message distribution.

## Relationships
* **Catalog Management** & **Circulation Engine** -> **PostgreSQL Database**: Reads and writes transactional data via native TCP drivers over TLS enforcing EU-only data residency.
* **Circulation Engine** -> **Event Publisher**: Communicates via in-process Spring Beans and direct method calls.
* **Event Publisher** -> **Message Broker**: Publishes domain events via AMQP over TLS.
* **Catalog Management** -> **Search Synchronizer**: Triggers indexing updates via direct method calls.
* **Search Synchronizer** -> **Search Engine**: Updates indices via native TCP drivers over TLS.

## Technology Stack
* **Java & Spring Boot**: Core runtime framework providing a modular monolith structure.
* **Spring Data JPA / Spring TX**: Manages data access and strict transactional boundaries.
* **Spring AMQP**: Handles asynchronous event publishing.
* **PostgreSQL Database**: Relational datastore ensuring strict EU data residency.
* **Search Engine (Elasticsearch)**: External search index ensuring high-performance catalog searches.

## Rationale
This modular monolith architecture keeps transactional integrity high using in-process Spring Beans while cleanly separating concerns. Bypassing the transactional database for search queries directly addresses the < 800 ms latency requirement (R-05) and respects EU data residency constraints.

Search Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Search Engine container provides high-performance catalogue discovery for the Library Management System. It enables rapid retrieval of physical and digital items while enforcing strict EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- **Query Parser**: Sanitizes and translates search requests using Elasticsearch Query DSL.
- **Indexing Worker**: Consumes synchronization events to update the index.
- **Search Index (Storage Node)**: Lucene-based storage node enforcing EU data residency.
- **Ranking & Relevance Tuner**: Applies custom scoring scripts and synonym mappings.

## Relationships
- Core Domain -> Query Parser: Submits search requests [HTTP/JSON over TLS via Elasticsearch Java Client]
- Message Broker -> Indexing Worker: Streams catalog sync events [AMQP]
- Query Parser -> Ranking & Relevance Tuner: Applies custom scoring and boosts [Internal Lucene API]
- Query Parser -> Search Index: Executes low-latency index lookups [Internal Java Transport / Lucene API]

## Technology Stack
- **Elasticsearch**: Chosen as the core search engine to achieve sub-800ms 99th-percentile search response times.
- **Lucene API**: Utilized internally for efficient indexing, scoring, and storage operations.
- **LUKS**: Implemented for disk encryption at rest to satisfy EU data residency constraints.
- **Elasticsearch Java Client**: Standardized for communication between the Core Domain and Query Parser over HTTP/TLS.

## Rationale
This component architecture meets the sub-800ms performance requirement through dedicated indexing and query parsing mechanisms. Additionally, it guarantees compliance with EU-only data residency via isolated storage nodes and localized disk encryption.

Integration Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for libraries. The Integration Worker container handles asynchronous tasks and external integrations within strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Message Consumer**: Subscribes to events from the Message Broker.
- **Payment Integrator**: Communicates with the Payment Gateway.
- **Notification Integrator**: Handles payload mapping and delivery to the Notification Service.
- **Retry & Dead-Letter Handler**: Manages transient failures and unprocessable messages.
- **Webhook Receiver**: Ingests asynchronous callbacks from external systems.

## Relationships
- Message Consumer -> Message Broker (RabbitMQ): Subscribes to events [AMQP]
- Payment Integrator -> Payment Gateway: Processes fine payments [HTTPS/REST]
- Notification Integrator -> Notification Service: Sends alerts [HTTPS/REST]
- Webhook Receiver -> Payment Gateway: Ingests callbacks [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js with TypeScript**: Selected for asynchronous I/O performance.
- **BullMQ**: Manages retry logic and job queues.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: Backs BullMQ and ensures EU-only data residency without external Redis.
- **Regional Endpoint Configurations**: Hardcoded in HTTP clients to enforce compliance.

## Rationale
This component architecture ensures high availability and reliable asynchronous processing for external services. It rigorously enforces EU data residency constraints by utilizing regional endpoints and local database-backed queues.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for libraries. It uses a component-level Message Broker architecture to handle asynchronous workflows and integrations.

## Key Elements
- **Exchange Router**: Directs incoming messages using RabbitMQ Direct/Topic Exchanges.
- **Queue Manager**: Manages durable message queues via RabbitMQ Quorum Queues.
- **Connection & Security Manager**: Handles authentication and TLS termination using TLS 1.3 and x.509/PLAIN auth.
- **Dead Letter Handler**: Captures failed messages using RabbitMQ Dead Letter Exchanges (DLX).

## Relationships
- **Core Domain -> Exchange Router**: Publishes domain events [AMQP 0-9-1 over TLS].
- **Exchange Router -> Queue Manager**: Routes events to queues [AMQP internal].
- **Queue Manager -> Integration Worker**: Delivers messages for processing [AMQP 0-9-1 over TLS].
- **Queue Manager -> Dead Letter Handler**: Forwards failed messages [AMQP internal].
- **Dead Letter Handler -> PostgreSQL Database**: Persists failed messages for audit/replay [JDBC over TLS].

## Technology Stack
- **RabbitMQ**: Message broker software for asynchronous decoupling and event routing.
- **RabbitMQ Quorum Queues**: Consensus replication to meet EU-only data residency and high availability constraints.
- **TLS 1.3**: Secure transport protocol ensuring encrypted communication.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: Relational database for persistent storage of failed messages.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high availability and robust asynchronous workflow failure handling while strictly adhering to EU-only data residency requirements. Consensus replication guarantees data safety across distributed nodes.

PostgreSQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It strictly adheres to EU-only data residency constraints while ensuring high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patron & Librarian**: End-users interacting via self-service portals.
- **Web Application**: React and TypeScript frontend container.
- **API Gateway**: Kong or NGINX routing layer.
- **Core Domain**: Java and Spring Boot backend container.
- **Search Engine**: Elasticsearch container for complex queries.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: EU-hosted relational database container housing the Relational Schema Engine, Full-Text Search Index (`pg_trgm`), Audit & Data Residency Enforcement Module, and Connection Pooler (PgBouncer).
- **Integration Worker**: Node.js or Python background worker.
- **Message Broker**: RabbitMQ container.

## Relationships
- **Core Domain** -> **Connection Pooler**: Manages pooled SQL transactions via JDBC over TLS 1.3.
- **Integration Worker** -> **Relational Schema Engine**: Performs asynchronous bulk updates via native PostgreSQL wire protocol.
- **Core Domain** -> **PostgreSQL Database**: Reads and writes transactional data using native TCP drivers over TLS.

## Technology Stack
- **React & TypeScript**: Powers the Web Application for type-safe UI development.
- **Java & Spring Boot**: Implements the Core Domain for robust business logic execution.
- **PostgreSQL**: Stores transactional data with strict geographic compliance and fast exact-match lookups.
- **PgBouncer**: Manages database connection limits to sustain peak transactional throughput.
- **Elasticsearch**: Handles high-performance search queries to meet the < 800 ms response requirement.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with EU data residency laws while delivering sub-800ms search responses through optimized indexing and connection pooling. Decoupled containers and robust protocols guarantee high scalability and transactional integrity.
